papers_new.title: A scalable dense silicon qubit architecture with logical operations
papers_new.abstract: Fault-tolerant quantum computing (FTQC) requires a large number of physical qubits to encode logical qubits with sufficiently low error rates. Silicon spin qubits are a promising platform because of their small footprint, compatibility with semiconductor manufacturing technologies, and demonstrated high-fidelity operations. However, realizing a scalable architecture that supports quantum error correction, qubit transport, wiring, and logical gate operations remains a major challenge. Here, we propose a scalable dense silicon spin qubit architecture designed to support large-scale FTQC. The architecture consists of qubit memories, data qubit lanes, and cross junctions. Qubit memories store logical qubits encoded using the rotated surface code and support logical single-qubit operations. Data qubit lanes enable high-speed one-dimensional spin shuttling for connectivity between logical…

papers_new.title: Froq: Safe Speculative Execution on Live Quantum States for FTQC
papers_new.abstract: Reducing execution time is critical to fault-tolerant quantum computing (FTQC) as longer executions expose logical qubits to more opportunities for failure. However, quantum processors could frequently stall due to slow classical error-correction decoders. Recent speculative decoding accelerates this process, but its speculation remains on the classical side, leaving quantum operations waiting for confirmed decoding results. Extending speculative execution to the quantum side is fundamentally challenging. Unlike classical processor states, quantum states cannot be arbitrarily copied or checkpointed for rollback, making recovery from mispredictions difficult. In this work, we propose Froq to enable safe speculative execution on live quantum states. Froq uses compiler-assisted recovery contracts to track how mispredictions propagate through quantum operations. It further employs a…

papers_new.title: Scaling classical hardware for accurate real-time quantum error correction
papers_new.abstract: Fault-tolerant quantum computation requires a classical decoder fast enough to process syndrome measurements at the rate at which they are generated, and to return its decisions with low latency. This is most demanding for superconducting processors, whose fast syndrome cycles force a trade-off between decoding speed and accuracy. Decoders fast enough to keep up sacrifice accuracy, which must be compensated for with larger codes and thus additional physical qubits. Here we introduce Rapids, a streaming neural decoder that is both fast and accurate. We achieve this by co-designing the decoder with a field-programmable gate array (FPGA): the network is built from operations that map cheaply onto the device and trained in its integer arithmetic. For the distance-19 surface code, Rapids decodes each round of syndromes in under a microsecond on a single FPGA, fast enough for superconducting…

papers_new.title: A measurement-free quantum error correction protocol for superconducting cavities
papers_new.abstract: The realization of large-scale quantum computation will require quantum error correction (QEC). One way to reduce the demands placed on QEC is to correct dominant physical errors at a lower level before passing the remaining errors to an outer code. Recently, Krastanov et al. [Nat. Commun. 12, 191 (2021)] proposed a measurement-free error-correction protocol based on coherent control of photonic modes that corrects for photon loss. Here, we adapt this approach to a circuit quantum electrodynamics (cQED) architecture using three superconducting microwave cavities coupled by Josephson-junction-based nonlinear elements. We encode the logical qubit in the lowest-order binomial code of one cavity, while the two other cavities serve as ancillas. Using numerical simulations with experimentally realistic parameters, we demonstrate that our protocol can correct single-photon loss with 99%…
papers_new.excerpt: The realization of large-scale quantum computation will require quantum error correction (QEC).

papers_new.title: QuFrame: Pauli Frame Tracking for Fault-Tolerant Quantum Control
papers_new.abstract: Fault-tolerant quantum computing requires continuous quantum error correction (QEC) to suppress physical noise. While Clifford-only workloads can defer corrections to software post-processing, universal computation breaks this paradigm: executing non-Clifford gates via magic-state gadgets introduces hard, real-time control-flow dependencies on error-corrected measurements. Consequently, the controller must extract syndromes, decode them, and update the Pauli frame in real time, closing the entire QEC loop within a strict $1\,μ\text{s}$ cycle. However, prior proposals on Pauli frame tracking remain largely theoretical, leaving the microarchitectural bottlenecks of tracking, resolving, and synchronizing frame updates across distributed control pipelines unaddressed. To this end, we present QuFrame, a control microarchitecture for real-time Pauli frame tracking that closes the QEC loop…

papers_new.title: General Noise Channels and Mid-Circuit Measurements for Pre-Trajectory Sampling with Batched Execution
papers_new.abstract: Many studies of quantum protocols require fast sampling of large amounts of measurement data from noisy quantum circuits, such as for training machine-learning decoders for quantum error correction. Exact simulation of realistic noise is expensive, while stabilizer-based simulators are fast but approximate, for example through Pauli twirling, which generally alters the output statistics. Pre-trajectory sampling with batched execution (PTSBE) accelerates exact trajectory simulation by sampling noise before state evolution. This method requires the outcome probability of every stochastic event to be independent of the state, which excludes mid-circuit measurements and general Kraus channels. We present a generalization of PTSBE to measurement and Kraus operators without approximation. Each event is partially pre-sampled, while deferred outcomes are drawn during grouped execution via…
papers_new.excerpt: Many studies of quantum protocols require fast sampling of large amounts of measurement data from noisy quantum circuits, such as for training machine-learning decoders for quantum error correction.

papers_new.title: Fault-tolerant quantum processor with minimal external control
papers_new.abstract: Contemporary classical information processors integrate tens of billions of transistors printed on a chip, yet are fully controlled through comparatively few external wires. This is possible because data flows through hard-coded operations in step with a global clock and is steered by external instructions. Today's solid-state quantum processors are different -- every qubit receives instructions from outside the chip via its own dedicated control line, and error correction adds a further torrent of syndrome data that is transported off-chip. Here we show that the external control of a quantum chip can be greatly simplified. We propose a fault-tolerant architecture for universal quantum computation, inspired by modern classical processors, in which quantum information flows through a fixed, clocked device, propelled by local gates in a planar array. Our quantum processor receives an…

papers_new.title: Teleportation of Logical Qubits using Lattice Surgery with Superconducting Circuits
papers_new.abstract: Demonstrating a quantum advantage when solving large-scale computational problems on a quantum computer requires the correction of errors that occur due to limitations in control accuracy and coherence. Using the concept of quantum error correction, fault-tolerant logical qubits can be realized and manipulated with logical single- and two-qubit gates. In this paper, we experimentally analyze fault-tolerant lattice-surgery, which is a key primitive that enables operations between logical qubits realized in the surface-code. Using this primitive, we demonstrate the teleportation of logical states between two distance-three logical qubits realized in a superconducting circuit composed of 41 physical qubits. Throughout this process, we study the step-by-step transfer of logical information from a source to a target logical qubit by characterizing the time evolution of logical observables.…

papers_new.title: Resolving and Suppressing Temporally Correlated Noise in Quantum Error Correction
papers_new.abstract: Scaling fault-tolerant quantum error correction (QEC) requires suppressing errors in both space and time, yet standard logical memory experiments primarily probe spatial faults. Here, we use a 105-qubit Willow superconducting quantum processor to realize and scale the surface code stability experiment, which is alternatively sensitive to temporal error chains. Scaling from patch sizes of $3 \times 3$ to $7 \times 7$, we realize a timelike block suppression factor of $μ_T = 1.47 \pm 0.25$, demonstrating the ability to maintain temporal error suppression as the number of qubits increases. By extending the stability experiment for many cycles, we uncover a sum-of-exponentials behavior in error suppression caused by a temporally correlated error: data-qubit heating to the third excited state $|3\rangle$. We fully capture this effect with a parameter-free, device-level leakage model…

papers_new.title: Evolving Decoding Algorithms for Quantum Error Correction
papers_new.abstract: Quantum computation entails robustness engineering: a noisy quantum state is measured continuously, and a classical algorithm (the decoder) must infer corrections that reliably remove the noise, fast enough to keep up. We write several published belief-propagation (BP) decoders for quantum low-density parity-check (qLDPC) codes in a Domain-Specific Language (DSL), and search over it with grammatical evolution. Written in the language, the published decoders show their parameters in plain view, allowing us to re-parameterise BP+OSD (ordered statistics decoding) and BP+LSD (localized statistics decoding) decoders with damping, before any search, making each 17.1--41.0$\times$ faster at a higher error rate, and BP+OSD-0 about 103 faster than the ldpc package's version tuned on the [[72,12,6]] bivariate-bicycle code. Evolution over the language finds decoders that improve the time-error…
papers_new.excerpt: Quantum computation entails robustness engineering: a noisy quantum state is measured continuously, and a classical algorithm (the decoder) must infer corrections that reliably remove the noise, fast enough to keep up.

papers_new.title: Amatlas: A 2D Array Architecture for Union-Find Decoding Without Global Coordination
papers_new.abstract: Real-time decoding of the surface code is essential for fault-tolerant quantum computing, and scaling the decoder to large code distances in hardware remains a challenge. The locality of Union-Find (UF) decoding makes it a leading candidate for such a decoder in distributed hardware. Prior distributed UF decoders, however, map the three-dimensional decoding graph onto an array of processing elements (PEs) under a central controller that synchronizes all PEs at every stage, and a three-dimensional array of PEs scales poorly on planar hardware. This paper presents Amatlas, a two-dimensional PE array for UF decoding that operates without a central controller. Amatlas assigns one PE to each stabilizer on the two-dimensional qubit lattice and stores the states of all measurement rounds in the local memory of the PE, so every link connects adjacent PEs in the array. papers_new.excerpt: Real-time decoding of the surface code is essential for fault-tolerant quantum computing, and scaling the decoder to large code distances in hardware remains a challenge.

papers_new.title: Using a static spacetime subsystem code to calculate Floquet code distance
papers_new.abstract: Dynamical codes, including Floquet codes, can capture time-dependent phenomena in quantum error correction circuits that are absent from static stabilizer or subsystem codes, such as detecting regions and error propagation. They are also capable of preserving more logical qubits than corresponding schemes in which the same syndrome-extraction measurements are performed without being distributed over time. However, evaluating the performance of dynamical codes is more complicated than for static codes because error detection depends on when an error occurs within the measurement schedule. In this work, we introduce a mapping from the measurement sequence of a Floquet code to a static spacetime subsystem code and show that calculating the distance of a Floquet code can be reduced to calculating the distance of the corresponding static subsystem code. papers_new.title: Quditology: harnessing many levels for quantum information processing
papers_new.abstract: Quantum computing offers the prospect of surpassing classical computation on certain tasks by leveraging quantum coherence and entanglement. However, a significant gap remains between current quantum hardware and the requirements to transcend what classical computers can achieve, with decoherence limiting the capacity of storing quantum information and the number of logical steps that can be executed reliably. In the long term, fault tolerance bridges this gap, but simply changing the numerical base from binary to higher base d is a viable way to 'squeeze more juice'---get more quantum information processing---from a quantum computer of given size. Additionally, for quantum simulations, qudits offer a natural encoding scheme for high-dimensional physical degrees of freedom. Here, we review recent experimental progress in high-fidelity preparation, control, and measurement of qudits…

papers_new.title: How Small Can a Single Shor Run Be? Limits and Constructions for secp256k1
papers_new.abstract: Most resource estimates for breaking secp256k1 with Shor's algorithm describe one long run per attempt, and the spacetime volume of that run, its peak number of logical qubits times its Toffoli count, sets its logical-error budget. Ekerå's tradeoff shrinks each run by using more runs, but how far it can shrink the largest run, and at what circuit cost, has not been determined. We minimize the volume of the largest run while every key is recovered with probability at least 0.99, within ten times the total volume of three runs of Häner et al.\ and $2^{40}$ classical operations. We prove that a linear run fixed in advance, which starts its group register at a point and discards its label, reveals at most $\log_2(1+(|S|-1)/r)$ bits about a uniform key, where $|S|$ counts its exponent values and $r$ is the group order. papers_new.title: All-electronic geometric phase gate on Doppler-cooled trapped ions using an axial mode
papers_new.abstract: We report the experimental demonstration of a high-fidelity oscillating magnetic gradient entangling gate on the axial stretch mode of a two-ion crystal in a micro-fabricated surface Paul trap, therefore allowing for mixed-species sympathetic cooling. With only Doppler-cooled $^{171}$Yb$^+$ ions at $\bar{n}$ = 50(5), we achieve Bell-state fidelities far above the relevant fault-tolerant threshold, simplifying transport protocols within a shuttling-based-architecture. The control fields consist only of an oscillating current applied to submerged integrated wires emitting a B-field gradient near-resonant with the axial mode, and resonant microwave pulses at the qubit frequency constituting very low gate calibration overheads. We also demonstrate an adiabatic elimination of spin-motion entanglement (AESE) version of the gate, showcasing significant robustness.

papers_new.title: Blueprint for DOE Quantum Supercomputing
papers_new.abstract: Quantum computing stands at the threshold of a transformative decade, where the field will evolve from small-scale demonstrations toward practical scientific computing at scale. This Blueprint identifies fault-tolerant quantum computers (FTQCs) as a viable, scalable, and broadly applicable path to achieving "quantum scientific utility." It outlines a strategy to prepare the US Department of Energy (DOE) for FTQCs and their integration into the US national scientific computing infrastructure. Its purpose is to identify the steps, milestones, and research directions necessary for DOE to enable initial deployment of FTQCs in 2028 as a scientific tool for the nation and mature this capability into the 2030s. Given recent demonstrations of logical operations on error-corrected logical qubits and the advancement of commercial hardware roadmaps, DOE should begin preparations for large-scale,…

papers_new.title: Reducing RSA-2048 Factoring Resources Below One Billion Toffolis via LLM-Driven Verifiable Quantum Compilation
papers_new.abstract: Modular exponentiation dominates the logical cost of factoring 2048-bit RSA integers (RSA-2048) with Shor's algorithm. Recent approaches based on approximate residue number systems (RNS) sharply reduce the required logical qubits, yet still demand billions of Toffoli gates. Optimizing these circuits is difficult because shared ancilla qubits and measurement-based uncomputation tightly couple the arithmetic stages, while rare overflows in compressed registers occur too infrequently for random simulation to detect. Here we use large language model (LLM)-driven search to redesign the RNS pipeline across stages and build a deterministic compiler that produces a Pareto frontier of RSA-2048 circuits. papers_new.title: Impact of structured noise on bosonic quantum error correction
papers_new.abstract: Bosonic quantum error correction relies on an accurate description of single-photon loss dissipation using an ideal annihilation operator, under which correctable loss errors act equivalently on different logical code states. In realistic weakly nonlinear bosonic modes, however, coupling to a structured environment can render photon loss Fock-state dependent, thereby modifying the effective dissipation operator and deforming the associated error space. Here, we experimentally investigate this effect in a three-dimensional circuit quantum electrodynamics system. By injecting spectrally engineered environmental noise into a weakly nonlinear oscillator, we observe pronounced frequency selectivity in the measured Fock-state dynamics. papers_new.title: Foliated surface codes for optimal skip-gate leakage correction
papers_new.abstract: Skip-gate leakage --- such as atom loss in neutral-atom arrays or trapped ions, or photon loss in superconducting dual-rail qubits --- takes a qubit out of its computational subspace and removes subsequent gates acting on it. If leakage is only detectable end-of-the-line at qubit measurement, error correction circuits must be designed to periodically measure all qubits, as in SWAP-based circuits and foliation. We show that the best SWAP-based surface code, although optimal against space-like skip-gate leakage errors, is suboptimal against time-like leakage errors. By optimal, we mean that the code corrects as many leakage errors as it can detect. Remarkably, we find that the foliated surface code is optimal against both space- and time-like error configurations. We support our findings with numerical simulations. Under two-qubit gate leakage with probability 0.5%, foliation suppresses…

papers_new.title: Non-Binary Detector Error Models
papers_new.abstract: A key challenge in fault-tolerant quantum error correction (QEC) is that the syndrome extraction circuits are themselves faulty. Such circuit-level noise is commonly described by a detector error model (DEM). In Stim and in almost all related works, DEMs are binary: every non-binary circuit error (e.g., CNOT gate), is decomposed into independent binary error mechanisms. In this work, we introduce non-binary DEMs, in which each fault location of the syndrome extraction circuit is modeled by one random variable over its original alphabet, e.g., the 16 two-qubit Pauli errors after a CNOT gate. We also propose a split-merge-regroup transformation that builds a compact non-binary DEM from any Clifford circuit by merging the error components that flip the same detectors and observables. Non-binary DEMs represent any Pauli channel exactly, whereas binary DEMs are exact only for channels that…
papers_new.excerpt: A key challenge in fault-tolerant quantum error correction (QEC) is that the syndrome extraction circuits are themselves faulty.

papers_new.title: Parallel transversal entangling gates for fault-tolerant trapped-ion quantum computing
papers_new.abstract: Fault-tolerant quantum computing requires high-fidelity entangling gates that can be implemented efficiently across multiple qubit pairs. We present a scheme for simultaneous pairwise entangling operations, i.e., a transversal controlled-$Z$ gate, across neighboring wells in a double-well trapped-ion architecture. A tailored dynamical decoupling scheme suppresses unwanted couplings with a pulse count that scales quadratically with the number of ions. We show that incorporating a genuine geometric cancellation reduces the pulse count and, for selected register sizes, allows the parallel operation to be completed faster than an equivalent sequence of two-qubit gates while requiring a significantly smaller two-photon Rabi frequency. We assess the experimental feasibility of the protocol by analyzing the impact of decoherence and crosstalk arising from laser wave-vector misalignment. To…
papers_new.excerpt: Fault-tolerant quantum computing requires high-fidelity entangling gates that can be implemented efficiently across multiple qubit pairs.

papers_new.title: Accelerating Quantum Error Correction Simulations under Coherent Noise with Compiled Clifford-Augmented Matrix Product States
papers_new.abstract: Reliable assessment of quantum error correction requires understanding how coherent errors affect logical performance. Although tensor networks naturally capture coherent interference, entanglement growth and large qubit counts make repeated sampling costly. Here we develop a compiled Clifford-Augmented Matrix Product State (CAMPS) framework that reuses Clifford transformations across shots, recycles qubits released by measurements, evolves a compressed residual state, and accelerates sampling through rotation fusion and compilation tailored to the MPS layout. Surface-code benchmarks under fixed-sign coherent noise yield accurate logical error estimates at small bond dimensions, while random-sign simulations up to distance $d=9$ and on the $[[72,12,6]]$ bivariate bicycle code match the Pauli-twirling approximation results. Compared with uncompiled CAMPS, compiled CAMPS converges at…

papers_new.title: Topological Quantum Reservoir Computing
papers_new.abstract: Scaling universal quantum computation and implementing quantum machine learning with protected logical qubits remain challenging. To harness the computational potential of existing fault-tolerant quantum platforms, we introduce topological quantum reservoir computing, a novel approach using protected degrees of freedom for storage and the host system's intrinsic dynamics for information processing. Using a one-dimensional Kitaev chain, we show how long-lived Majorana edge modes and fast bulk responses support these complementary functions within the same many-body system. We identify the tradeoffs governing access to protected memory and show how matched interfaces enable programmable writing and interactions enable autonomous information consolidation from the bulk to the edge. These mechanisms improve performance on tasks requiring long-term retention of temporal information. Our…

papers_new.title: High-rate low-distance color codes
papers_new.abstract: Experimental implementations of two-dimensional color codes encoding a single logical qubit have surpassed the fidelity of physical qubits. A natural next step is to investigate higher-rate codes that encode multiple logical qubits. Here we propose small, high-rate 2D color codes for this purpose. We design distance-$3$ codes with encoding rates up to $1/3$ and distance-$4$ codes with encoding rates up to $1/4$. We prove that these rates are optimal for color codes with only color boundaries on surfaces with non-negative Euler characteristic. We benchmark the codes by simulating Steane-style error correction with real-time feedback and no post-selection in a linear trapped-ion chain model with all-to-all connectivity. The two best-performing codes have parameters $[[20,4,4]]$ and $[[16,4,4]]$ and achieve break-even at two-qubit gate infidelities of $0.22\%$ and $0.26\%$, respectively.…

papers_new.title: CHEQ: A Concurrent Hardware Evaluation Platform for QEC Decoders via Batch-Invariant Circuit-Level Noise Sampling
papers_new.abstract: Hardware quantum error correction (QEC) decoders require validation of logical error suppression and timing compliance before deployment. Rare logical failures and deadline violations demand extensive sampling, while algorithm-level software evaluation does not directly measure hardware response times. Circuit-level noise models contain many error mechanisms but few firings per shot at low physical error rates, making exhaustive per-shot scanning inefficient. We present CHEQ, an FPGA platform integrating on-chip sampling, concurrent decoder evaluation, scoring, and RISC-V control. Its Sampling Units use geometric skipping to sample firing locations from detector error models and amortize mechanism traversal across shots within each batch. Under independent random draws and exact geometric sampling, the shot distribution is invariant to batch size, enabling a memory-throughput tradeoff.…

papers_new.title: MASQ: Measurement-Adaptive Sampling for Near-Clifford Quantum Error Correction Circuits
papers_new.abstract: Classical sampling of quantum error correction (QEC) circuits supports fault-tolerant protocol evaluation, but estimating rare logical failures requires many independent shots. Frame-active-state simulators isolate non-stabilizer information in a dense active-state vector, yet dense-state processing remains exponential in the active width. This paper presents MASQ, an exact measurement-adaptive sampler for near-Clifford QEC circuits based on selective materialization of non-Clifford rotations. At each measurement boundary, MASQ materializes only rotations in a measurement-relevant closure capturing direct and indirect non-commuting dependencies, deferring the rest to limit active-state expansion. papers_new.title: Magic state cultivation with lattice-surgery escape on superconducting hardware
papers_new.abstract: Magic state cultivation (MSC) is a low-overhead protocol for fault-tolerantly preparing logical magic states. In this work, we implement two MSC variants to prepare a magic state in a distance-5 code on a publicly available IBM Nighthawk processor. The first is a lattice-surgery escape, recently proposed by Hirano et al. and experimentally studied here for the first time. The second is a grafting escape, previously demonstrated by Rosenfeld et al., and extended here by incorporating a switch into a matchable code. Both protocols begin with fault-tolerant cultivation of a T state on a color code, followed by an escape into a larger code. We decode the results using minimum-weight perfect matching or Tesseract on circuit-level error models calibrated to the hardware noise. papers_new.title: Probing the real-time decoding accuracy bounds in trapped ion architectures
papers_new.abstract: Fault tolerant quantum computers will rely on real-time decoders that process syndromes faster than the QEC cycle duration. The millisecond cycle times offered by trapped ion platforms relax low-latency decoding demands, but simulations and experiments have not yet exploited this time budget to reach maximum logical error suppression. We show how a hybrid sliding window decoding scheme composed of a lower-accuracy and a higher-accuracy decoder can yield substantially improved logical error rates, while preserving low latency. All windows are handled by the lower-accuracy decoder, with some windows being infrequently switched to the higher-accuracy decoder. We extract soft-output information from the lower-accuracy decoder efficiently for any QLDPC code, which allows us to identify decoding windows of low confidence. papers_new.title: Exponential Quantum Memory Advantage for Late-Graph Smoothness and Spectral Estimation
papers_new.abstract: Graph signal processing tests how smoothly the decisions of next-generation massive sensor networks with $N$ nodes vary over their neighbour graph. Memory becomes the bottleneck when the neighbour graph arrives only after data erasure, a late-graph setting motivated by dispersed sensor networks and telemetry. We analyse three collection scenarios, reliable rounds, continuous broadcast and ordered capture, and test the Dirichlet energy $\mathcal E_G=\mathbf z^{\mathsf T}\mathbf L\mathbf z/N$ of the fused decision map $\mathbf z\in\{\pm1\}^N$, with late-graph Laplacian $\mathbf L$, against two thresholds. Hidden Matching uses $O(\log N)$ qubits on fused bits, but in reliable rounds and continuous broadcast, where nodes report $b$ sub-bits separately, a classical record buffer before it uses $O(N b)$ bits; classical methods need $Ω(\sqrt N)$ bits in the worst case. papers_new.title: Quantum Algorithm for Direct Estimation of Energy-Level Differences via Quantum Dynamics Simulation
papers_new.abstract: We present a quantum algorithm for the early fault-tolerant quantum computing (early-FTQC) era that estimates minute energy-level differences, such as energy gradients and molecular forces, at a lower sampling cost than existing phase-estimation methods. Such energy derivatives, accessed as the small energy difference induced by an infinitesimal parameter shift, are central to quantum simulation in chemistry and materials science. Although Statistical Phase Estimation (SPE) is well-suited to energy estimation in this era, applying it to an energy difference demands a sampling complexity that scales with the operator norm of the full Hamiltonian, which grows with system size. papers_new.title: Reproducible distributions of energy-relaxation times in superconducting qubits from broadband SWAP spectroscopy
papers_new.abstract: The distribution of the qubit energy-relaxation time (T1) in a superconducting quantum processor affects its logical error rates. However, reports on qubit fabrication quality focus on the median or best-case T1 from measurements that are not reproducible due to resonant coupling to two-level system (TLS) defects whose frequencies fluctuate in time. Here, we sweep the frequency f01 of a flux-tunable qubit over several GHz with SWAP spectroscopy, quoting the quality factor Q = 2 pi f01 T1 to make T1 comparable across frequencies. We show that the cumulative distribution of Q pooled over the sweep is reproducible across four thermal cycles spanning 326 days, up to the reshuffling of strongly coupled TLSs. In contrast to repeated measurements at a single frequency, the medians of the broadband Q distributions spread by an order of magnitude less over 3 days. The distance between the…

papers_new.title: Reducing T gates in product formulas with agent loops
papers_new.abstract: Quantum chemistry calculations on a fault-tolerant quantum computer usually require many $\text{T}$ gates. This cost depends on the simulation method and how precisely its rotations are implemented. In this paper, we used Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, a large language model (LLM), in a coding-agent loop to optimize the structure and rotation-synthesis precision of product formulas (PFs) for quantum phase estimation (QPE). Each of five independent searches optimized a shared protocol across 115 HamLib molecular Hamiltonians spanning 4--16 qubits over 100 code mutations. The searches started from a calibrated, nested second-order PF with uniform synthesis precision. We minimized $T_{95}$, the estimated total $\text{T}$-gate cost including QPE queries and repeated attempts for $95\%$ success probability, while requiring chemical accuracy for every training Hamiltonian. papers_new.title: Exploiting SU(2) Symmetry for Efficient Quantum State Preparation of Matrix Product States
papers_new.abstract: Quantum computing offers a promising route to simulating strongly correlated systems, particularly for dynamical and spectral quantities whose classical computation can become prohibitively expensive. Fault-tolerant algorithms for these tasks, including real-time dynamics and phase estimation, assume efficient preparation of the initial many-body state, making state preparation an important bottleneck. Matrix product states obtained classically with the density matrix renormalization group can be compiled sequentially into fault-tolerant circuits. We exploit non-Abelian spin SU(2) symmetry in this compilation. By the Wigner-Eckart theorem, only the reduced tensors, which carry the variational information, need generic unitary synthesis. The magnetic structure is restored by Clebsch-Gordan transformations with analytically known angles. We benchmark the method on representative strongly…
papers_new.excerpt: Quantum computing offers a promising route to simulating strongly correlated systems, particularly for dynamical and spectral quantities whose classical computation can become prohibitively expensive.

papers_new.title: Quantum Capacity with Incoherent Codes
papers_new.abstract: Arbitrarily weak depolarizing noise drives the quantum capacity to zero in every input basis when the encoder is restricted to incoherent operations. Even one qubit cannot then be sent reliably: if the output is replaced by the maximally mixed state with probability $\varepsilon\le1/2$, the entanglement fidelity is at most $1-\varepsilon/2$ at every block length. With unrestricted decoding, a single-letter formula gives the capacity with incoherent encoding as the maximum Holevo information over ensembles of basis states with identical environment outputs. For either incoherent or unrestricted encoding, imposing incoherent decoding reduces the capacity by at most a factor of two; this factor is optimal. We bound the fidelity of incoherent decoders and evaluate the capacities with incoherent encoding for multiqubit Pauli channels.
papers_new.excerpt: Arbitrarily weak depolarizing noise drives the quantum capacity to zero in every input basis when the encoder is restricted to incoherent operations.

papers_new.title: Second-order asymptotics for the quantum and private capacities of the erasure channel
papers_new.abstract: An erasure channel either delivers a quantum system intact or tells the receiver that it was lost. How much quantum information, or secret classical information, can a finite block transmit without assistance? We determine the optimal second-order coding rates for input dimension $d\ge2$, erasure probability $0<p<1/2$, and fixed infidelity (one minus fidelity) $0<\varepsilon<1$. For $n$ channel uses, the optimal base-two logarithmic code size is \begin{equation}\tag{A}\label{eq:abstract-rate} n(1-2p)\log_2d +2\sqrt{np(1-p)}\log_2d\,Φ^{-1}(\varepsilon) +O((\ln n)^2), \end{equation} where $Φ$ is the standard normal cumulative distribution function and $Φ^{-1}$ is its quantile function. The square-root term is the second-order correction. This formula holds for entanglement transmission, entanglement generation, and private classical communication. Quantum error measures failure to…
papers_new.excerpt: An erasure channel either delivers a quantum system intact or tells the receiver that it was lost.

papers_new.title: Schur saturation and the Clifford ceiling in qudit CSS codes
papers_new.abstract: Orthogonality-type conditions (triorthogonality in the qubit setting and its prime-dimensional analogues), are the primary algebraic screening criterion for transversal non-Clifford gate constructions in CSS codes. In every known positive construction the certificate is accompanied by a non-Clifford logical gate, leaving open whether a CSS family can satisfy these conditions to arbitrarily high order while admitting no such gate. We answer this question for the class of symmetric spectral CSS codes $Q(A)=CSS(C(A),C(A))$ built from character evaluation on a finite abelian group $G$ with $\exp(G)\mid p-1$, $p\geq 5$ prime. The mechanism is the identity \[C(A)^\perp * C(A)^\perp=\mathbb{F}_p^G,\] which we call Schur saturation of the dual code. It follows from the CSS self-orthogonality condition $A\cap(-A)=\varnothing$ and annihilates every local polynomial phase of degree $\geq 3$. The…
papers_new.excerpt: Orthogonality-type conditions (triorthogonality in the qubit setting and its prime-dimensional analogues), are the primary algebraic screening criterion for transversal non-Clifford gate constructions in CSS codes.

papers_new.title: Neural Decoding of Logical Clifford Circuits with Transversal Gates
papers_new.abstract: On neutral-atom and trapped-ion machines, a transversal gate needs only one syndrome round, so a logical gate takes up to d times less time than with lattice surgery. However, transversal gates make decoding harder, because a transversal CNOT copies errors between two blocks of physical qubits, so a decoder must read all blocks of a circuit together. Algorithmic decoders for such circuits gain accuracy at the cost of speed. Neural decoders ease this trade-off, but they must infer from data where errors go across each gate and how logical outcomes propagate through the circuit, although both are known exactly. In this work, we present Duet, a neural decoder for logical Clifford circuits with transversal gates that builds in this known information and learns only which errors occurred. Duet leverages three insights. First, each transversal gate moves an error to a fixed place, so the…
papers_new.excerpt: On neutral-atom and trapped-ion machines, a transversal gate needs only one syndrome round, so a logical gate takes up to d times less time than with lattice surgery.

papers_new.title: Advancing the Theory of Pretty Good Quantum Operations
papers_new.abstract: Finding optimal quantum measurements or recovery maps is often demanding. Pretty good measurements and Petz maps offer explicit approximations achieving at least the square of optimal performance by the Barnum-Knill bound. We unify these operations in a semidefinite programming framework with a tunable power, extending them to broader quantum tasks. We prove a stronger bound for powers above one up to three that peaks at quadratic power. For structured channels such as stabilizer codes under Pauli noise, large powers steer recovery to a maximum likelihood decoder for maximally mixed inputs.
papers_new.excerpt: Finding optimal quantum measurements or recovery maps is often demanding.

papers_new.title: Resilience of Entangling Gates to Spatiotemporally Correlated Noise
papers_new.abstract: As quantum processors scale, spatially and temporally correlated noise is emerging as a limiting factor in the fidelity of multiqubit gates. Here we show that this makes the choice of entangling operation a first-order design decision: for two-qubit gates in semiconductor spin qubits, the CZ and $\sqrt{\mathrm{iSWAP}}$ gates exhibit a pronounced resilience to correlated noise relative to the SWAP gate, even though correlated fluctuations of the entangling interaction can degrade gate performance to a level comparable to that of local noise. We trace this hierarchy to the redistribution of noise-sensitive channels away from zero frequency and show it to hold for noise spectra dominated by low-frequency weight, including $1/f$ and Lorentzian. These results follow from a general expression, derived here, for the average gate infidelity under arbitrary spatiotemporal noise correlations,…
papers_new.excerpt: As quantum processors scale, spatially and temporally correlated noise is emerging as a limiting factor in the fidelity of multiqubit gates.

papers_new.title: Mitigating drift in spin-qubit control with calibration-insensitive pulses
papers_new.abstract: Silicon spin qubits offer fault-tolerant control fidelities in a platform that is compatible with commercial foundries, but device calibration drifts and control parameters must be retuned every few hours. Here, we replace conventional square control pulses with two drift-resilient pulse families: the adiabatic BIR-4 and the composite CORPSE. In a Si/SiGe quantum-dot device, we benchmark single-qubit gate sets built from each pulse against deliberate miscalibration. We find that BIR-4 offers a 99% Clifford fidelity over a factor of 2 change in drive power and CORPSE maintains similar fidelity over +/-0.9MHz of offset. When fully calibrated CORPSE offers a 99.97% fidelity per gate, on par with a calibrated square pulse. Starting with tuned pulses, we then track errors using gate-set tomography for ten days without recalibration. BIR-4 holds its rotation angle to 0.3 degrees throughout,…
papers_new.excerpt: Silicon spin qubits offer fault-tolerant control fidelities in a platform that is compatible with commercial foundries, but device calibration drifts and control parameters must be retuned every few hours.

papers_classic.title: Surface codes: Towards practical large-scale quantum computation
papers_classic.abstract: This article provides an introduction to surface code quantum computing. We first estimate the size and speed of a surface code quantum computer. We then introduce the concept of the stabilizer, using two qubits, and extend this concept to stabilizers acting on a two-dimensional array of physical qubits, on which we implement the surface code. We next describe how logical qubits are formed in the surface code array and give numerical estimates of their fault tolerance. We outline how logical qubits are physically moved on the array, how qubit braid transformations are constructed, and how a braid between two logical qubits is equivalent to a controlled-not. We then describe the single-qubit Hadamard, $\stackrel{\ifmmode \hat{}\else \^{}\fi{}}{S}$ and $\stackrel{\ifmmode \hat{}\else \^{}\fi{}}{T}$ operators, completing the set of required gates for a universal quantum computer. We…
papers_classic.excerpt: This article provides an introduction to surface code quantum computing.

papers_classic.title: Superconducting quantum circuits at the surface code threshold for fault tolerance
Quantum error correction for quantum memories
papers_classic.abstract: It may seem inevitable that highly entangled quantum states are susceptible to disturbance through interaction with a decohering environment. However, certain multiqubit entangled states are well protected from common forms of decoherence as the quantum information is hidden in inherently nonlocal degrees of freedom. This review shows that this robustness is enabled by specific measurements on subsets of qubits, implementing a quantum version of an error correction process. Beginning with the basics, the latest understanding of the relation between this form of error correction and the concept of two-dimensional topological order in many-body physics is reviewed.
papers_classic.excerpt: It may seem inevitable that highly entangled quantum states are susceptible to disturbance through interaction with a decohering environment.

papers_classic.title: Quantum error correction below the surface code threshold
papers_classic.abstract: Quantum error correction1-4 provides a path to reach practical quantum computing by combining multiple physical qubits into a logical qubit, in which the logical error rate is suppressed exponentially as more qubits are added. However, this exponential suppression only occurs if the physical error rate is below a critical threshold. Here we present two below-threshold surface code memories on our newest generation of superconducting processors, Willow: a distance-7 code and a distance-5 code integrated with a real-time decoder. The logical error rate of our larger quantum memory is suppressed by a factor of Λ = 2.14 ± 0.02 when increasing the code distance by 2, culminating in a 101-qubit distance-7 code with 0.143% ± 0.003 per cent error per cycle of error correction. This logical memory is also beyond breakeven, exceeding the lifetime of its best physical qubit by a factor of 2.4 ±…
papers_classic.excerpt: Quantum error correction1-4 provides a path to reach practical quantum computing by combining multiple physical qubits into a logical qubit, in which the logical error rate is suppressed exponentially as more qubits are…

papers_classic.title: Suppressing quantum errors by scaling a surface code logical qubit
papers_classic.abstract: Practical quantum computing will require error rates well below those achievable with physical qubits. Quantum error correction1,2 offers a path to algorithmically relevant error rates by encoding logical qubits within many physical qubits, for which increasing the number of physical qubits enhances protection against physical errors. However, introducing more qubits also increases the number of error sources, so the density of errors must be sufficiently low for logical performance to improve with increasing code size. Here we report the measurement of logical qubit performance scaling across several code sizes, and demonstrate that our system of superconducting qubits has sufficient performance to overcome the additional errors from increasing qubit number. We find that our distance-5 surface code logical qubit modestly outperforms an ensemble of distance-3 logical qubits on average,…
papers_classic.excerpt: Practical quantum computing will require error rates well below those achievable with physical qubits.

papers_classic.title: Surface code quantum computing by lattice surgery
papers_classic.abstract: In recent years, surface codes have become a leading method for quantum error correction in theoretical large-scale computational and communications architecture designs. Their comparatively high fault-tolerant thresholds and their natural two-dimensional nearest-neighbour (2DNN) structure make them an obvious choice for large scale designs in experimentally realistic systems. While fundamentally based on the toric code of Kitaev, there are many variants, two of which are the planar- and defect-based codes. Planar codes require fewer qubits to implement (for the same strength of error correction), but are restricted to encoding a single qubit of information. Interactions between encoded qubits are achieved via transversal operations, thus destroying the inherent 2DNN nature of the code. In this paper we introduce a new technique enabling the coupling of two planar codes without…
papers_classic.excerpt: In recent years, surface codes have become a leading method for quantum error correction in theoretical large-scale computational and communications architecture designs.

papers_classic.title: Bulk locality and quantum error correction in AdS/CFT
papers_classic.abstract: We point out a connection between the emergence of bulk locality in AdS/CFT and the theory of quantum error correction. Bulk notions such as Bogoliubov transformations, location in the radial direction, and the holographic entropy bound all have natural CFT interpretations in the language of quantum error correction. We also show that the question of whether bulk operator reconstruction works only in the causal wedge or all the way to the extremal surface is related to the question of whether or not the quantum error correcting code realized by AdS/CFT is also a “quantum secret sharing scheme”, and suggest a tensor network calculation that may settle the issue. Interestingly, the version of quantum error correction which is best suited to our analysis is the somewhat nonstandard “operator algebra quantum error correction” of Beny, Kempf, and Kribs. Our proposal gives a precise…
papers_classic.excerpt: We point out a connection between the emergence of bulk locality in AdS/CFT and the theory of quantum error correction.

papers_classic.title: Realizing repeated quantum error correction in a distance-three surface code
Quantum error correction for beginners
papers_classic.abstract: Quantum error correction (QEC) and fault-tolerant quantum computation represent one of the most vital theoretical aspects of quantum information processing. It was well known from the early developments of this exciting field that the fragility of coherent quantum systems would be a catastrophic obstacle to the development of large-scale quantum computers. The introduction of quantum error correction in 1995 showed that active techniques could be employed to mitigate this fatal problem. However, quantum error correction and fault-tolerant computation is now a much larger field and many new codes, techniques, and methodologies have been developed to implement error correction for large-scale quantum algorithms. In response, we have attempted to summarize the basic aspects of quantum error correction and fault-tolerance, not as a detailed guide, but rather as a basic introduction. The…
papers_classic.excerpt: Quantum error correction (QEC) and fault-tolerant quantum computation represent one of the most vital theoretical aspects of quantum information processing.

papers_classic.title: A Game of Surface Codes: Large-Scale Quantum Computing with Lattice Surgery
papers_classic.abstract: Given a quantum gate circuit, how does one execute it in a fault-tolerant architecture with as little overhead as possible? In this paper, we discuss strategies for surface-code quantum computing on small, intermediate and large scales. They are strategies for space-time trade-offs, going from slow computations using few qubits to fast computations using many qubits. Our schemes are based on surface-code patches, which not only feature a low space cost compared to other surface-code schemes, but are also conceptually simple~--~simple enough that they can be described as a tile-based game with a small set of rules. Therefore, no knowledge of quantum error correction is necessary to understand the schemes in this paper, but only the concepts of qubits and measurements.
papers_classic.excerpt: Given a quantum gate circuit, how does one execute it in a fault-tolerant architecture with as little overhead as possible?

papers_classic.title: Real-time quantum error correction beyond break-even
Realization of three-qubit quantum error correction with superconducting circuits
Quantum error correction in a solid-state hybrid spin register
Quantum error correction of a qubit encoded in grid states of an oscillator
Application of a Resource Theory for Magic States to Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computing
papers_classic.abstract: Motivated by their necessity for most fault-tolerant quantum computation schemes, we formulate a resource theory for magic states. First, we show that robustness of magic is a well-behaved magic monotone that operationally quantifies the classical simulation overhead for a Gottesman-Knill-type scheme using ancillary magic states. Our framework subsequently finds immediate application in the task of synthesizing non-Clifford gates using magic states. When magic states are interspersed with Clifford gates, Pauli measurements, and stabilizer ancillas-the most general synthesis scenario-then the class of synthesizable unitaries is hard to characterize. Our techniques can place nontrivial lower bounds on the number of magic states required for implementing a given target unitary. Guided by these results, we have found new and optimal examples of such synthesis.
papers_classic.excerpt: Motivated by their necessity for most fault-tolerant quantum computation schemes, we formulate a resource theory for magic states.

papers_classic.title: Quantum error correction: an introductory guide
papers_classic.abstract: Quantum error correction protocols will play a central role in the realisation of quantum computing; the choice of error correction code will influence the full quantum computing stack, from the layout of qubits at the physical level to gate compilation strategies at the software level. As such, familiarity with quantum coding is an essential prerequisite for the understanding of current and future quantum computing architectures. In this review, we provide an introductory guide to the theory and implementation of quantum error correction codes. Where possible, fundamental concepts are described using the simplest examples of detection and correction codes, the working of which can be verified by hand. We outline the construction and operation of the surface code, the most widely pursued error correction protocol for experiment. Finally, we discuss issues that arise in the practical…
papers_classic.excerpt: Quantum error correction protocols will play a central role in the realisation of quantum computing; the choice of error correction code will influence the full quantum computing stack, from the layout of qubits at the…

papers_classic.title: Quantum Error Correction in Scrambling Dynamics and Measurement-Induced Phase Transition
papers_classic.abstract: We analyze the dynamics of entanglement entropy in a generic quantum many-body open system from the perspective of quantum information and error corrections. We introduce a random unitary circuit model with intermittent projective measurements, in which the degree of information scrambling by the unitary and the rate of projective measurements are independently controlled. This model displays two stable phases, characterized by the volume-law and area-law scaling entanglement entropy in steady states. The transition between the two phases is understood from the point of view of quantum error correction: the chaotic unitary evolution protects quantum information from projective measurements that act as errors. A phase transition occurs when the rate of errors exceeds a threshold that depends on the degree of information scrambling. We confirm these results using numerical simulations and…
papers_classic.excerpt: We analyze the dynamics of entanglement entropy in a generic quantum many-body open system from the perspective of quantum information and error corrections.

papers_classic.title: Realization of Real-Time Fault-Tolerant Quantum Error Correction
papers_classic.abstract: Correcting errors in real time is essential for reliable large-scale quantum computations. Realizing this high-level function requires a system capable of several low-level primitives, including single-qubit and two-qubit operations, mid-circuit measurements of subsets of qubits, real-time processing of measurement outcomes, and the ability to condition subsequent gate operations on those measurements. In this work, we use a ten qubit QCCD trapped-ion quantum computer to encode a single logical qubit using the $[[7,1,3]]$ color code, first proposed by Steane~\cite{steane1996error}. The logical qubit is initialized into the eigenstates of three mutually unbiased bases using an encoding circuit, and we measure an average logical SPAM error of $1.7(6) \times 10^{-3}$, compared to the average physical SPAM error $2.4(8) \times 10^{-3}$ of our qubits. We then perform multiple syndrome…
papers_classic.excerpt: Correcting errors in real time is essential for reliable large-scale quantum computations.

papers_classic.title: The Ryu–Takayanagi Formula from Quantum Error Correction
Realization of an Error-Correcting Surface Code with Superconducting Qubits
papers_classic.abstract: Quantum error correction is a critical technique for transitioning from noisy intermediate-scale quantum devices to fully fledged quantum computers. The surface code, which has a high threshold error rate, is the leading quantum error correction code for two-dimensional grid architecture. So far, the repeated error correction capability of the surface code has not been realized experimentally. Here, we experimentally implement an error-correcting surface code, the distance-three surface code which consists of 17 qubits, on the Zuchongzhi 2.1 superconducting quantum processor. By executing several consecutive error correction cycles, the logical error can be significantly reduced after applying corrections, achieving the repeated error correction of surface code for the first time. This experiment represents a fully functional instance of an error-correcting surface code, providing a key…
papers_classic.excerpt: Quantum error correction is a critical technique for transitioning from noisy intermediate-scale quantum devices to fully fledged quantum computers.

papers_classic.title: Fault-Tolerant Measurement-Based Quantum Computing with Continuous-Variable Cluster States
papers_classic.abstract: A long-standing open question about Gaussian continuous-variable cluster states is whether they enable fault-tolerant measurement-based quantum computation. The answer is yes. Initial squeezing in the cluster above a threshold value of 20.5 dB ensures that errors from finite squeezing acting on encoded qubits are below the fault-tolerance threshold of known qubit-based error-correcting codes. By concatenating with one of these codes and using ancilla-based error correction, fault-tolerant measurement-based quantum computation of theoretically indefinite length is possible with finitely squeezed cluster states.
papers_classic.excerpt: A long-standing open question about Gaussian continuous-variable cluster states is whether they enable fault-tolerant measurement-based quantum computation.

papers_classic.title: The XZZX surface code
papers_classic.abstract: Performing large calculations with a quantum computer will likely require a fault-tolerant architecture based on quantum error-correcting codes. The challenge is to design practical quantum error-correcting codes that perform well against realistic noise using modest resources. Here we show that a variant of the surface code-the XZZX code-offers remarkable performance for fault-tolerant quantum computation. The error threshold of this code matches what can be achieved with random codes (hashing) for every single-qubit Pauli noise channel; it is the first explicit code shown to have this universal property. We present numerical evidence that the threshold even exceeds this hashing bound for an experimentally relevant range of noise parameters. Focusing on the common situation where qubit dephasing is the dominant noise, we show that this code has a practical, high-performance decoder and…
papers_classic.excerpt: Performing large calculations with a quantum computer will likely require a fault-tolerant architecture based on quantum error-correcting codes.

papers_classic.title: Achieving the Heisenberg limit in quantum metrology using quantum error correction
papers_classic.abstract: Quantum metrology has many important applications in science and technology, ranging from frequency spectroscopy to gravitational wave detection. Quantum mechanics imposes a fundamental limit on measurement precision, called the Heisenberg limit, which can be achieved for noiseless quantum systems, but is not achievable in general for systems subject to noise. Here we study how measurement precision can be enhanced through quantum error correction, a general method for protecting a quantum system from the damaging effects of noise. We find a necessary and sufficient condition for achieving the Heisenberg limit using quantum probes subject to Markovian noise, assuming that noiseless ancilla systems are available, and that fast, accurate quantum processing can be performed. When the sufficient condition is satisfied, a quantum error-correcting code can be constructed that suppresses the…
papers_classic.excerpt: Quantum metrology has many important applications in science and technology, ranging from frequency spectroscopy to gravitational wave detection.

papers_classic.title: Repeated quantum error detection in a surface code
Low-distance surface codes under realistic quantum noise
papers_classic.abstract: Experimental implementation of the surface code will be a significant milestone for quantum computing. We develop a circuit and a decoder targeted for near-term implementation of a distance-3 surface code. We simulate the code under amplitude and phase damping and compare the threshold to a Pauli-twirl approximation. We find that the approximation yields a pessimistic threshold estimate. From numerical Monte Carlo simulations, we identify the gate and measurement speeds required to achieve reliable error correction. For superconductor devices, a qubit encoded in a 17-qubit surface code demonstrates a lower error rate than an unencoded qubit assuming gate times of 5--40 ns and ${T}_{1}$ times of at least 1--2 $\ensuremath{\mu}\mathrm{s}$. If ${T}_{1}\ensuremath{\ge}10$ ns, the difference is significant and can be experimentally measured, allowing near-term implementation and verification…
papers_classic.excerpt: Experimental implementation of the surface code will be a significant milestone for quantum computing.

papers_classic.title: Quantum error correction and universal gate set operation on a binomial bosonic logical qubit
Quantum Error Correction for Metrology
papers_classic.abstract: We propose and analyze a new approach based on quantum error correction (QEC) to improve quantum metrology in the presence of noise. We identify the conditions under which QEC allows one to improve the signal-to-noise ratio in quantum-limited measurements, and we demonstrate that it enables, in certain situations, Heisenberg-limited sensitivity. We discuss specific applications to nanoscale sensing using nitrogen-vacancy centers in diamond in which QEC can significantly improve the measurement sensitivity and bandwidth under realistic experimental conditions.
papers_classic.excerpt: We propose and analyze a new approach based on quantum error correction (QEC) to improve quantum metrology in the presence of noise.

papers_classic.title: Erasure conversion for fault-tolerant quantum computing in alkaline earth Rydberg atom arrays
papers_classic.abstract: Executing quantum algorithms on error-corrected logical qubits is a critical step for scalable quantum computing, but the requisite numbers of qubits and physical error rates are demanding for current experimental hardware. Recently, the development of error correcting codes tailored to particular physical noise models has helped relax these requirements. In this work, we propose a qubit encoding and gate protocol for 171Yb neutral atom qubits that converts the dominant physical errors into erasures, that is, errors in known locations. The key idea is to encode qubits in a metastable electronic level, such that gate errors predominantly result in transitions to disjoint subspaces whose populations can be continuously monitored via fluorescence. We estimate that 98% of errors can be converted into erasures. We quantify the benefit of this approach via circuit-level simulations of the…
papers_classic.excerpt: Executing quantum algorithms on error-corrected logical qubits is a critical step for scalable quantum computing, but the requisite numbers of qubits and physical error rates are demanding for current experimental…

papers_classic.title: Improved Quantum Metrology Using Quantum Error Correction
papers_classic.abstract: We consider quantum metrology in noisy environments, where the effect of noise and decoherence limits the achievable gain in precision by quantum entanglement. We show that by using tools from quantum error correction this limitation can be overcome. This is demonstrated in two scenarios, including a many-body Hamiltonian with single-qubit dephasing or depolarizing noise and a single-body Hamiltonian with transversal noise. In both cases, we show that Heisenberg scaling, and hence a quadratic improvement over the classical case, can be retained. Moreover, for the case of frequency estimation we find that the inclusion of error correction allows, in certain instances, for a finite optimal interrogation time even in the asymptotic limit.
papers_classic.excerpt: We consider quantum metrology in noisy environments, where the effect of noise and decoherence limits the achievable gain in precision by quantum entanglement.

papers_classic.title: Quantum Error Correction with Only Two Extra Qubits
papers_classic.abstract: Noise rates in quantum computing experiments have dropped dramatically, but reliable qubits remain precious. Fault-tolerance schemes with minimal qubit overhead are therefore essential. We introduce fault-tolerant error-correction procedures that use only two extra qubits. The procedures are based on adding "flags" to catch the faults that can lead to correlated errors on the data. They work for various distance-three codes. In particular, our scheme allows one to test the ⟦5,1,3⟧ code, the smallest error-correcting code, using only seven qubits total. Our techniques also apply to the ⟦7,1,3⟧ and ⟦15,7,3⟧ Hamming codes, thus allowing us to protect seven encoded qubits on a device with only 17 physical qubits.
papers_classic.excerpt: Noise rates in quantum computing experiments have dropped dramatically, but reliable qubits remain precious.
